source_block.parva: Stri Parva (vulgate §10–§27; BORI CE ch. 9–27): Jalapradanika sub-parva (Dhritarashtra and the Kuru women set out; Vyasa restrains Gandhari; Kunti, Draupadi and Gandhari), Stri-vilapa sub-parva (Vyasa's boon of divine sight; Gandhari's lament; her curse on Krishna and his acceptance), Shraddha sub-parva (the funeral rites; the water-offerings at the Ganga; Kunti reveals Karna; Yudhishthira's offering to Karna)
source_block.bori: BORI CE Stri Parva ch. 9–27, Debroy translation vol. 8 (chapter-group citations): Dhritarashtra sets out with Gandhari, Kunti and the women; Vyasa restrains Gandhari (dharma and victory); Yudhishthira with joined hands, Gandhari's forgiveness; Kunti, Draupadi and Gandhari; Vyasa's boon of divine sight; Gandhari's lament to Krishna and her curse (the thirty-sixth year); Krishna's smiling acceptance; the funeral rites; the water-offerings at the Ganga; Kunti's revelation of Karna; Yudhishthira's water-rite for Karna.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, vulgate numbering = Ganguli): Stri Parva, Jalapradanika Parva adhyayas 10 (prasthan), 14–15 (Vyasa restrains Gandhari; Kunti, Draupadi, Gandhari); Stri-vilapa Parva adhyayas 16 (divya drishti), 25 (shaap and Krishna's sweekriti); Shraddha Parva adhyayas 26 (daah-sanskar), 27 (jalanjali; Karna-janm rahasya).
source_block.divergence: Section/adhyaya numbers follow the vulgate (Ganguli = Gita Press); BORI CE chapters are cited at chapter-group level only, and the CE sub-parva boundaries differ slightly from the vulgate's. Omitted for length: Vidura's and Sanjaya's consolations (§1–§9), the meeting with Kripa, Ashwatthama and Kritavarma on the road, the iron image of Bhima that Dhritarashtra crushes (§12–§13), Gandhari's exchange with Bhima, her glance through the blindfold at Yudhishthira's toe, the long lament over each fallen warrior (§16–§25), Krishna's rebuke of Gandhari (§26), the numbers of the slain, and Yudhishthira's curse on women's secrets (later, Shanti Parva). In the texts Gandhari sees the field from afar by Vyasa's boon and then all go to it; the plate shows her at its edge. The fires are lit by Vidura, Sanjaya, Sudharma, Dhaumya and Yuyutsu at Yudhishthira's command; the rites plate shows only Yudhishthira and Dhritarashtra at prayer before lamps, the fires as a distant glow. Yudhishthira offers water to Karna together with Karna's family; the offering plate shows Kunti and Draupadi watching.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: Dhritarashtra comes to the field with Gandhari, Kunti and the Kuru women; Vyasa reminds Gandhari of 'where dharma is, there is victory' and she forgives the Pandavas; Kunti raises Draupadi and Gandhari comforts them; Vyasa's boon of divine sight; Gandhari's curse on Krishna (the thirty-sixth year, his own clan) and his smiling acceptance; the funeral rites for all the slain at Dhritarashtra's word and Yudhishthira's command; the water-offerings at the Ganga; Kunti's revelation that Karna was the eldest brother; Yudhishthira's water-rite for Karna. Ganguli for English wording.
